title: 第八章　明天会更好，明天？气候危机与增长的托词

zh: 第八章　明天会更好，明天？气候危机与增长的托词
en: 8 A Better Tomorrow, Tomorrow? Climate Crisis and the Alibi of Growth

zh: 气候灾难要求我们发展新的概念——关于自由与政治、关于人与非人世界、关于代际和民族之间的正义——以便为应对不断展开的危机提供更好的工具。但这场灾难也要求我们解释政治上的失败：为什么未能及时行动。为什么现有的集体生活概念显得如此不受批评影响？有一个概念因其对反复提出的重塑或抛弃呼吁的抵抗而格外突出：经济观念。在无数关于气候政治的批评文本中，我们被敦促逃离经济及其狭隘的福祉定义，以更具生态意识的物质需要和限度概念取而代之，并与其无限增长的逻辑决裂。但经济观念——作为把握和衡量我们物质生活的一种方式——以及公众对其持续增长的执念，在很大程度上对这些批评免疫。为什么会这样？
en: The climate catastrophe demands that we develop new conceptions – of freedom and the political, of the human and nonhuman worlds, of justice between generations and peoples – to provide better tools for coping with the unfolding crisis. But the catastrophe also asks us to account for the political failure to have acted in time. Why have existing conceptions of collective life appeared so impervious to critique? One concept stands out for its resistance to repeated calls for its recasting or abandonment: the idea of the economy. In countless critical texts on climate politics, we are urged to escape from the economy, with its narrow definition of well-being, to replace it with a more ecological conception of our material needs and limits, and to break with its logic of limitless growth. But the idea of the economy, as a way of grasping and measuring our material life, and the public preoccupation with its continued growth, have been largely immune to such criticisms. Why is that so?

zh: 答案有两方面。第一，我们一直缺乏对经济所做之事的理解。经济通常被理解为所有现代社会的一种自然特征，指物质生产和交换的领域。我们常常被告知，它需要得到更好的管理，以更好的方式衡量，从而更准确地捕捉社会不公和生态危害的形式。相反，经济应被视为一种装置或技术设备，一种作为臣服模式运作的东西——或者，我要借用福柯对杰里米·边沁全景敞视监狱的解读，称之为“经济全景装置”（EconoCon）。作为一种装置，经济被格式化的方式有助于生产政治
臣服和集体主体性的形式，使当下的少数人能够以未来大多数人为代价生活——包括，正如本书所论证的，多数人如今受制于偿还此前从未来榨取的款项这一义务，这笔债务多数人必须持续且日益沉重地承担。
en: The answer is twofold. First, we have lacked an understanding of what the economy does. The economy is usually understood as a natural feature of all modern societies, designating the sphere of material production and exchange. It needs to be better managed, we are often told, and measured in better ways, to more accurately capture forms of social injustice and ecological harm. The economy should be seen instead as an apparatus or technical device, one that operates as a mode of subjection – or what I shall call, with a nod to Foucault’s reading of Jeremy Bentham’s Panopticon, the ‘EconoCon’. As a device, the economy is formatted in ways that help produce the forms of political

subjection and collective subjectivity that enable a minority in the present to live at the expense of most people in the future – including, as this book has argued, their subjection today to the repayment of previous extractions from the future, a debt the majority must continually and increasingly bear.

zh: 第二，我们一直缺乏对增长的理解。对多数人来说，经济增长显得是资本主义社会的自然运动，由不可避免的技术进步过程或过去资本不断积累、寻求进一步扩张机会所驱动。它几乎从不与资本化、或资本主义从未来榨取的模式联系起来。相反，我们不应把增长问题当作一种历史力量来处理——一种为避免比全球变暖已经预示的更灾难性后果而必须以某种方式加以限制或逆转的力量——而应把它当作一种偿付保障机制。增长是一种确保债务偿还的装置。这种思路并不会使增长对集体福祉的破坏性减少。但它确实使我们能够把增长理解为并非历史发展或资本主义扩张的必然运动，而是一种较近期的安排，它产生于——而非仅仅导致——我们从未来榨取的模式。
en: Second, we have lacked an understanding of growth. For most people, economic growth appears as the natural movement of capitalist society, driven by an ineluctable process of technological improvement or a continuous accumulation of capital from the past seeking further opportunities for expansion. It is almost never connected to capitalisation, or the capitalist mode of extraction from the future. Instead, we should approach the question of growth not as a historical force – one that, if we are to avoid even more calamitous consequences than those that global warming already has in store, we must somehow limit or reverse – but as a mode of indemnification. Growth is a device for securing the repayment of debt. This approach does not make growth any less damaging to collective well-being. But it does allow us to grasp it not as the inevitable movement of historical development or capitalist expansion, but as a more recent arrangement that arises from – rather than simply causing – our mode of extraction from the future.

zh: 第三项论点从这两点中产生。在解释经济增长加速的现象时，我们误解了化石燃料的作用。它们在引发气候紧急状态中的作用毋庸置疑。但经济装置及其增长执念，与碳基能源使用的增加之间是什么关系？在这里，我们关于经济是所有现代社会共有的物质生活领域、其增长是资本主义自然扩张的平常观念，再次妨碍我们理解气候危机和我们对化石燃料的依赖。
en: A third argument emerges from these two. In explaining the phenomenon of accelerating economic growth, we have misunderstood the role of fossil fuels. Their role in causing the climate emergency is not in question. But what is the relation between the device of the economy and our preoccupation with its growth, on the one hand, and the increasing use of carbon-based energy, on the other? Here, again, our ordinary idea of the economy as the sphere of material life common to all modern societies, and of its growth as an expansion natural to capitalism, stands in the way of understanding the climate crisis and our dependence on fossil fuels.

zh: 让我们从碳基能源及其与增长的关系这一问题开始，然后转向经济以及如何理解它在管理从未来榨取之模式中的作用。最后，我们将回到一种不同的理解：化石燃料与经济，以及作为资本托词的增长。
en: Let us begin with this question of carbon-based energy and its relation to growth, then turn to the economy and how to understand its role in managing modes of extraction from the future. We will return at the end to a different understanding of fossil fuels, the economy, and growth as an alibi of capital.

zh: 经济及其增长
en: The Economy and Its Growth

zh: 化石燃料时代由增长观念所界定。但什么是增长，它与碳能源有什么关系？我们如何开始相信，燃烧化石燃料创造了一个集体世界，而这个世界的界定特征就是增长？如果我们想要一个没有增长的世界，或具有不同增长形式、对地球系统和物种破坏较少的世界，我们必须追问：增长如何与化石燃料的榨取和燃烧联系在一起？
en: The era of fossil fuels has been defined by the idea of growth. But what is growth and how is it related to carbon energy? How did we come to believe that burning fossil fuels created a collective world whose defining character has been to grow? If we want a world without growth, or with a different form of growth, less destructive of Earth systems and species of life, we must ask how growth came to be associated with the extraction and burning of fossil fuels.

zh: 答案乍看显而易见。如本书前几章所探讨的，过去两个世纪里，煤炭以及后来石油和天然气的开发，提供了集中且迅速增加的能源来源，为制造业、工业化农业、机械化战争、城市扩张以及贸易和帝国的领土扩张提供动力。这种增长可以被衡量为某种物质的东西。它表现为不断扩大的商品数量、建筑数目、运输里程、人口规模和资本主义生产控制下的领土面积。
en: The answer seems at first obvious. Over the last two centuries, as earlier chapters of this book explored, the exploitation of coal and later oil and natural gas made available a concentrated and rapidly increasing source of energy that fuelled manufacturing, industrial agriculture, mechanised warfare, the expansion of cities, and the territorial enlargement of trade and empire. This growth could be measured as something material. It appeared in the form of the expanding quantities of goods, numbers of buildings, miles of transportation, size of populations, and areas of territory under the control of capitalist production.

zh: 但这个显而易见的答案并不有用。它误解了能源的历史，也误解了经济增长的本质。它带有技术决定论的毛病，仿佛历史本来不可能有其他样子——仿佛它是由人类进步和技术发展的不可避免性所驱动的。我们无法在此基础上建立应对气候危机的政治。
en: But the obvious answer is not a useful one. It misunderstands both the history of energy and the nature of economic growth. It suffers from a technical determinism, as if history could not have been otherwise – as if it were driven by the very unavoidability of human progress and technical development. We cannot build a politics to address the climate crisis on these terms.

zh: 相反，让我们从可以说气候危机开始的地方开始，不是两百年前，而是二十世纪中叶。这场危机与过去六七十年的大加速有着特殊关系，因而与我们加速的化石燃料消费有着特殊关系，尤其与 1990 年代以来最近三十年更快的加速有关。自工业时代开始以来燃烧的所有化石燃料中，超过 80% 是 1960 年以后燃烧的，所有燃烧量的一半以上是 1990 年以后燃烧的。
但“经济”的增长与化石燃料及大气碳生产扩大之间的这种关系，需要一种新的解释。
en: Let us begin, instead, where the climate crisis itself can be said to begin, not 200 years ago but in the mid-twentieth century. The crisis has a particular relationship to the great acceleration of the last six or seven decades, and thus to our accelerated consumption of fossil fuels, and especially to the more rapid acceleration of just the last three decades, since the 1990s. More than 80 per cent of all fossil fuels burned since the start of the industrial age have been burned since 1960, and more than half of them since 1990.
But that relation – between the growth of ‘the economy’ and the expanding production of fossil fuels and atmospheric carbon – needs a new explanation.

zh: 我们不应把增长问题定位于化石燃料的燃烧，也不应定位于需要化石燃料的技术装置（如蒸汽机、发电站或汽车）的历史，而应定位于另一种技术装置的发明：经济。正如我们在
所见，经济学家直到 1930 年代才开始使用“the economy”（作为对象的经济整体）这一说法（“economy”一词
不带定冠词使用时的旧含义非常不同，如

所解释的）。它到 1950 年代才广泛使用。统计学家设计了一套协议和假定，用来估算这个新对象的规模和扩张，概括起来就是国内生产总值即 GDP 的衡量。经济不只是已经存在之物的新词。它标示了一个新的政治和计算对象，第一次被理解为自身存在的实体，一个由可识别、可衡量的关系组成的稳定领域。这一装置组装得如此迅速，以至于到 1950 年代中期，经济学家、政治学家和历史学家开始想象“经济”一直存在，尽管他们不过在一二十年前才得知它的存在。
en: We should locate the problem of growth not in the burning of fossil fuels or the history of technical apparatuses that demanded them, such as the steam engine, the electrical power station, or the automobile, but in the invention of a different technical apparatus, the economy. As we saw in
, economists began to use the term ‘the economy’ only in the 1930s (older meanings of the word ‘economy’,
used without the definite article, as

explained, were very different). It came into widespread use only in the 1950s. Statisticians devised a set of protocols and assumptions for estimating the size and expansion of this new object, summarised as the measurement of the gross domestic product, or GDP. The economy was not just a new word for what already existed. It designated a new object of politics and calculation, understood for the first time as an entity in itself, a stable domain composed of identifiable and measurable relations. So rapidly was this device assembled that, by the mid-1950s, economists, political scientists, and historians started to imagine that ‘the economy’ had always existed, even though they had learned of its existence only ten or twenty years before.

zh: 应当指出，经济这一对象的出现主要发生于欧美。当欧洲人和美国人开始围绕本国经济的生产和衡量来管理政治生活时，并非每个国家都一开始同意跟随。这些分歧可能影响深远。如

所述，1956 年苏伊士危机由阿斯旺高坝融资争端引发，导致以色列、英国和法国入侵埃及、试图推翻其政府，部分就是一场关于新经济计算形式的分歧——帝国列强通过世界银行要求埃及政府采用这些形式。渐渐地，世界银行和其他国际机构要求全球南方国家采用这些方法，以产生看似可比的 GDP 数字和其他经济生活衡量指标。但这些衡量的适当性和可比性始终有待质疑。而且，通过衡量和管理经济及其增长来治理人口的方式，在不同地方并未采取相同形式或具有相同意义。
en: The emergence of the economy, it should be noted, was largely a Euro-American story. When Europeans and Americans started managing their political life around the production and measurement of their economy, not every country agreed at first to follow. These disagreements could be far-reaching. As

noted, the 1956 Suez Crisis, triggered by a dispute over the financing of the Aswan High Dam, and leading to the invasion of Egypt by Israel, Britain, and France in an attempt to remove its government from power, was, in part, a disagreement over the new forms of economic calculation that the imperial powers, through the World Bank, demanded that the Egyptian government adopt. Gradually, the World Bank and other international institutions required the countries of the Global South to adopt the methods that produced what seemed comparable figures for GDP and other measures of economic life. But the suitability and comparability of these measurements was always open to question. And the mode of governing populations through the measurement and management of the economy and its growth did not take the same form or significance in different places.

zh: GDP 不是物质财富的衡量。它衡量的是货币通过账户的流通。账户有三类：企业、政府和家庭。家庭被想象为微型企业，各有年度收入、支出和利润水平——一种剩余，被误导性地视为经济借以扩张的“投资”或“资本”来源，其假定是资本乃过去储蓄之物，而非从未来榨取。这些账户被呈现为统计抽象，因而是一种再现，但它再现的不是物质财富，而是收入。从较早计算国民

财富的尝试转向计算总收入，似乎引入了一种分离——增长衡量与物质扩张之间的分离。随着经济的发明，一个国家如今可以在不扩张领土、不增加人口、甚至也许不生产更多物质商品的情况下实现“增长”。人们或许以为这种脱钩会引起对增长观念的质疑。但恰恰相反，资本主义现代性不是由扩张与收缩、贫困化与改善的周期、而是由无休止、不间断、指数增长的逻辑所界定的观念，变得自明。无止境的经济增长成为政治福祉和进步的衡量标准本身。
en: The GDP is not a measure of material wealth. Rather, it measures the circulation of money through accounts. The accounts are of three kinds: those of business firms, government, and households. Households are imagined as miniature businesses, each with an annual level of income, expenditure, and profit – a surplus that is seen misleadingly as the source of ‘investment’ or ‘capital’ through which the economy expands, on the assumption that capital is something saved from the past, not extracted from the future. The accounts are presented as a statistical abstraction, and thus as a representation, and not of material wealth, but of income. The change from older attempts to calculate national

wealth to the calculation of gross income appeared to introduce a separation – between the measurement of growth and physical expansion. With the invention of the economy, a country could now ‘grow’ without expanding its territory, enlarging its population, or even, perhaps, producing more material goods. One might expect this decoupling to raise questions about the idea of growth. But, on the contrary, the notion that capitalist modernity was defined not by cycles of expansion and contraction, of impoverishment and improvement, but by the logic of endless, uninterrupted, and exponential growth became self-evident. Economic growth without end became the very measure of political well-being and progress.

zh: 从一开始，开始应用这些新指标体系的统计学家、规划者和预算官员就意识到其局限。无限指数增长的观念荒谬，甚至仅从数学上看也是如此。画成图表曲线，代表经济增长的上升线迅速接近垂直。如

所述，其荒谬性通过采用对数尺度绘制纵轴（显示 GDP 增长）的惯例而部分被掩盖。对数图把上升曲线变成一条平缓得多的直线，使其路径显得几乎合理。GDP 计算方式的缺陷也被注意到。这些缺陷的清单长得惊人，并日益为人熟悉。几十年来，赫尔曼·戴利等生态经济学家、凯西·吉布森和朱莉·格雷厄姆等女性主义学者、让·加德雷和弗洛朗丝·雅尼-卡特里丝等发展替代财富衡量的异端经济学家，以及许多其他人，都探讨过这些问题。
最近，乔治·卡利斯、杰森·希克尔和其他几位学者的一系列重要著作提出了去增长观念，或“优先考虑福祉、公平与可持续性”的以更少的物质消耗过好生活的方式，以此作为与把增长当作集体生活目标之做法决裂的手段。
en: From the start, the statisticians, planners, and budget officials who began to apply these new metrics were aware of their limitations. The idea of infinite exponential growth is absurd, even just mathematically. Drawn as the curve of a graph, the ascending line that represents the growth of the economy rapidly approaches the vertical. As mentioned in

, its absurdity was partially disguised by adopting the convention of plotting the vertical axis, showing the increase in GDP, on a logarithmic scale. The log plot converted an ascending curve into a straight and much flatter line, making its path appear almost reasonable. Flaws in the way GDP is calculated were also noted. The list of these is astonishingly long, and increasingly familiar. Over several decades, ecological economists such as Herman Daly, feminist scholars such as Kathy Gibson and Julie Graham, heterodox economists developing alternative measures of wealth such as Jean Gadrey and Florence Jany-Catrice, and many others, have explored these issues.

More recently, an important series of works by Giorgos Kallis, Jason Hickel, and several others have proposed the idea of degrowth, or modes of living well with less, by ‘prioritizing wellbeing, equity and sustainability’, as a means of breaking with the use of growth as the goal of collective life.

zh: 正如这些著作所指出的，GDP 作为福祉衡量是失败的：它排除大部分无酬劳动，尤其是持家、育儿和人类再生产的劳动——一种性别化、种族化的排除；它把有害支出也算作对繁荣的贡献，例如成瘾性或不健康消费，或军费开支、警察暴力和监禁的成本——因而第二次被种族化。它不重视闲暇，除非闲暇被付费。它不重视货物的可靠性或对浪费的避免，也不计入减少生产性资产价值的磨损。它把医疗和心理治疗支出
、维持极端不平等的财产和收入获取渠道所需的法律服务和会计程序支出，以及修复全球变暖后果造成的损害支出，都当作正面因素——而且这样做时，没有充分评价那些可能来自更好照护个人、社群或地球的改善。除资源储量逐渐减少时开采成本上升之外，它不赋予有限资源耗竭任何价值。它也不对生物多样性丧失、物种灭绝或其他地球生命代价进行估值，除非这些代价已由人类对过程或材料的控制主张作为金融资产定价。
en: As these works point out, GDP fails as a measure of well-being: it excludes most unpaid labour, in particular the labour of householding, childcare, and human reproduction – a gendered and racialised exclusion; it includes as contributions to prosperity harmful expenses, such as addictive or unhealthy consumption or the cost of arms spending, police violence, and incarceration – so is racialised a second time. It does not value leisure, except when this is paid for. It does not value the reliability of goods or the avoidance of waste, or account for the wear and tear that reduces the value of productive assets. It treats as positive

the expenditure on medical treatment and psychological care; on the legal services and accounting procedures required to maintain grossly unequal access to property and income; and on repairing damage from the effects of global heating – and it does this in ways that do not adequately value improvements that might have arisen from better provision for care of the person, the community, or the planet. It attributes no value to the exhaustion of finite resources, beyond the increased cost of extraction as reserves are run down. And it includes no valuation of the loss of biodiversity, of species extinction, or other costs to life on Earth beyond those priced by human claims to the control of processes or materials as financial assets.

zh: 半个多世纪前，正统经济学家已被迫回应环保主义者的批评，他们为该衡量的有用性辩护。威廉·诺德豪斯和詹姆斯·托宾在 1972 年写道，如果 GDP 未能衡量环境和其他成本，那是由于“价格体系的缺陷”。补救办法将是生产更好的价格。至于“全球生态灾难”的危险，他们补充说，例如“我们将融化极地冰盖、淹没世界所有海港”的风险，对于“此类事件的原因和可能性似乎存在极大不确定性”。因此他们提出，“单靠经济学能说的非常少”。
正统经济学家能够以确定性谈论经济，依赖于生产这种必要的不确定性和无知。
en: Orthodox economists, already forced to respond more than half a century ago to criticisms from environmentalists, defended the usefulness of the measure. If GDP failed to measure environmental and other costs, this was due to ‘a defect of the pricing system’, wrote William Nordhaus and James Tobin in 1972. The remedy would be to produce better prices. As for the danger of ‘global ecological catastrophes’, they added, such as the risk ‘that we will melt the polar icecaps and flood all the world’s seaports’, there seemed to be ‘great uncertainty about the causes and likelihood of such occurrences’. As a result, they proposed, there was ‘very little that economics alone can say’.
The certainty with which orthodox economists could speak about the economy was dependent on producing this necessary uncertainty and ignorance.

zh: 这些长期为人熟知的衡量经济及其增长的缺陷，使我们对这一概念的正常化更加不可思议。这些缺陷可以与第二种对经济增长的批评区分开来，后者通常更紧密地依托马克思主义思想传统：增长作为对自然日益加剧的榨取。
en: These long-familiar shortcomings in the measurement of the economy and its growth make our normalisation of the concept even more remarkable. Such flaws can be distinguished from a second kind of criticism of economic growth, usually drawing more closely on Marxian traditions of thought: growth as the increasing extraction from nature.

zh: 对后者来说，增长问题不在于衡量或错误衡量的实践，不在于我们如何评价或贬低自然和其他非经济物品，而在于资本主义的底层本质。在这种观点的许多版本中——南希·弗雷泽或杰森·摩尔的著作就是好例子——资本主义的独特之处在于其榨取主义。
资本主义作为组织关系的特定模式而产生和扩张，这种关系不仅存在于人类之间，也存在于人类与自然世界之间。如果把资本主义理解为通过支配劳动生产商品来扩张价值和占有剩余，那么它依赖于把材料加工成商品的无限扩张。资本主义通过进一步的空间扩张和加强对自然材料的开发
来解决自身危机；自然提供了不断扩张的储备，被视为“廉价”或免费的馈赠——阿丽莎·巴蒂斯托尼探讨过政治思想中的这一主题。
既然资本无情地寻求自我扩张，资本主义就依赖物质增长，而增长总是以自然资源为代价。无论怎样重新定义 GDP 或更好地衡量成本，都无法使资本主义摆脱这种破坏性、不可持续的自然关系。增长不是再现和评价资源方式不当的问题。它是资本主义生产方式底层的剥削动力。
en: For the latter, the problem of growth lies not in practices of measurement or mismeasurement, of how we value or disvalue nature and other noneconomic goods, but in the underlying nature of capitalism. What distinguishes capitalism, in many versions of this view – the work of Nancy Fraser or Jason Moore would be good examples – is its extractivism.

Capitalism came into being and expands as a specific mode of organising the relationship, not only among humans, but between humans and the natural world. If capitalism is understood as the expansion of value and appropriation of surplus through the command of labour to produce commodities, this depends on the endless expansion of the processing of materials into goods. Capitalism addresses its own

crises through further spatial expansion and increased exploitation of materials from nature, which provide a constantly expanding reserve of what it treats as ‘cheap’ or free gifts – a theme in political thought that Alyssa Battistoni has explored.

Since capital relentlessly seeks its own self-expansion, capitalism depends upon material growth, and growth is always at the expense of natural resources. No amount of redefinition of GDP or better measurement of costs will free capitalism from this destructive and unsustainable relationship to nature. Growth is not a problem of improper ways of representing and valuing resources. It is the exploitative dynamic at the base of the capitalist mode of production.

zh: 经济的效果
en: The Effect of the Economy

zh: 我们可以把这两种增长研究路径概括为一个问题：以 GDP 衡量的“经济”是一种
的再现，还是
一种再现。一边是那些人——例如有影响力的凯特·拉沃斯——主张我们应以替代性福祉计算取代以 GDP 衡量的增长指标，不一定反增长，但至少不预设支持或反对增长的立场。
另一边是资本理论家——近例可参见后殖民历史学家安德鲁·萨托里——他们认为二十世纪的“经济”概念相对不重要，因为它
是一种再现。萨托里主张，这可以与另一种观念过程相对照，即“抽象”，特别是所谓实在抽象——劳动、财产、价值——它们主要出现于十九世纪，对资本的运作至关重要。
en: One could summarise the two approaches to growth as a question of whether ‘the economy’ as measured by GDP is a
representation, or a

representation. On one side are those – for example, the influential Kate Raworth – who propose that we should replace the metric of growth, as measured by GDP, with alternative calculations of wellbeing, and become, not necessarily anti-growth, but at least agnostic about it.

On the other side, the theorists of capital – see the postcolonial historian Andrew Sartori for a recent example – who suggest that the twentieth-century conception of ‘the economy’ is relatively unimportant, because it is

a representation. It can be contrasted, he argues, with a different kind of ideational process, that of ‘abstraction’ and specifically the so-called real abstractions – labour, property, value – that emerged mainly in the nineteenth century and are fundamental to the working of capital.

zh: 无论采取哪一边，这场争论中双方的立场都有一个弱点，而且是同一个弱点。他们主张，经济虽然指涉某种真实的东西，但它是一种再现。或者说，它是一种再现、一种纯粹的约定，
它指涉别的某种东西，指涉一种物质现实——物质生产过程。
en: Whichever side one takes, both positions in this argument suffer from a weakness – and the same one. While it refers to something real, they argue, the economy is a representation. Or rather, it is a representation, a mere convention,
it refers to something else, to a material reality – to a process of material production.

zh: 尽管这些论点很有力量，这里所遵循的都不是。它们都没有考察“经济”为何如此晚近才被发明、它做了什么工作，或其政治臣服和控制的形式。经济既不是多数主流学术所设想的那种描绘物质现实的方式，也不是其（错误）再现、一种（错误衡量的）统计的纯粹产物。相反，正如
所考察的，它是
一种制造物质世界与其再现相对立这一
的特定方式：即以实体与金融对立的形式，或以物质世界与仅仅指涉它、管理它的账户、价格和金融交换体系相对立的形式。这种效果，这种安排事物与表象的秩序模式，这种装置或图表，正是资本主义的、或者说资本化攫取模式得以运作的机制。
en: Despite their power, neither of these arguments is the one followed here. Neither examines the reason why ‘the economy’ was invented so recently, the work it does, or its form of political subjection and control. The economy is neither a way of depicting a material reality, as most mainstream scholarship assumes, nor its (mis)representation, a mere product of (mismeasured) statistics. It is, rather, as
examined,
a specific way of producing the

of the material world versus its representation: namely in the form of the real versus the financial, or the material world and the system of accounts, prices, and financial exchanges that merely reference it and manage it. This effect, this mode of ordering things and appearances, this apparatus or diagram, is precisely the mechanism through which the capitalist, or rather the capitalising, mode of capture has come to operate.

zh: 注意这里使用的两个术语：“效果”和“资本化”。“效果”比抽象之类更宏大的术语更有用，部分原因是它能把我们的注意力引向许多细小、看似微不足道的技术政治实践——例如政府办公室里金融统计的汇编，或在此前时代大型零售公司收银机的记账；或者如
所述，银行业从“产业”中逐渐分离的过程：两者起初是商人生活中相互关联的两个方面，后来才在建筑、立法和职业层面彼此分离。“效果”兼有纯粹表象和实效性的含义。它使我们注意抽象与它所抽象之物之间始终不稳定的差异——而“抽象”一词一旦不再用作表示过程的动词性名词，通常无法做到这一点。
en: Note the use of two terms here, ‘effect’ and ‘capitalising’: the term ‘effect’ is more useful than a grander term like abstraction, partly because it can direct our attention to many of the minor, seemingly insignificant technopolitical practices – for example, the compilation of financial statistics in government offices, or, in a previous era, the record keeping by cash registers of large retail companies; or, as

recounted, the gradual process by which banking houses were separated from ‘industry’, architecturally, legislatively, and professionally, after starting as two interconnected aspects of merchant life. The term ‘effect’ carries the meaning of both mere appearance and effectiveness. It draws our attention to the always unstable difference between an abstraction and what it abstracts from – something the term abstraction, once it ceases to be used as a verbal noun indicating a process, usually fails to do.

zh: 这一论点与先前关于国家作为一种效果的论点相似。
但它有所不同，因为效果的生成方式不同。与国家的效果相比，经济的效果以不同方式治理我们。虽然经济像国家或社会一样是另一种抽象模式——我们通过指称它的捷径而看不到其组装过程——但有一种抽象化、构造差异的效果是经济生产所特有的。在这种模式的特殊性质中，我们必须理解并拆解增长问题。
en: This argument is analogous to one made previously about the state, as an effect.

But it is different, because the effect is produced differently. We are governed differently by the effect of the economy, compared with the effect of the state. While the economy is yet another mode of abstracting, like state, or society, whose process of assembling we fail to see in the shortcut of referencing it, there is an effect of abstracting, of constructing differences, that is particular to the production of the economy. In the specifics of that mode, we have to understand and disassemble the question of growth.

zh: 第二，“资本化”一词。如常一样，我们的目标是取代指涉大型对象或结构（如资本主义）的术语，代之以描述反复过程的词语（如资本化）。指称大型、看似难以改变的结构会强化抽象的力量，而关注平凡、重复的程序则能把注意力引向脆弱之处或潜在的中断点。如本书通篇所示，“资本化”指剩余攫取的模式，这种模式不应被理解为对自然的掠夺，甚至也不应被理解为对劳动本身的掠夺，尽管它可能同时利用这两种资源及其他资源：它是对未来的掠夺。把一项资产资本化，是指
确立对未来延伸的收入流——租金、购买付款、利润、费用、利息等等——控制权的政治—法律模式，然后在当下以折扣价榨取这些收入，从而使未来贫困化，让未来承担全额偿还的负担。
en: Second, the term capitalising. Our aim, as always, is to replace terms that refer to large objects or structures, like capitalism, with words that describe repetitive processes, such as capitalising. Referencing large, seemingly intractable structures reinforces the powers of abstraction, whereas focusing on mundane, reiterative procedures can draw attention to points of vulnerability or potential disruption. As seen throughout this book, the term ‘capitalising’ refers to the mode of capture of surplus, understood not as predation upon nature, nor even upon human labour per se, although it may make use of both resources, and of others: it is predation upon the future. To capitalise an asset refers to

the politico-legal mode of establishing control of flows of revenue stretching into the future – rents, purchases, profits, fees, interest payments, and more – and then extracting them at a discounted price in the present, thereby impoverishing the future, on which the burden of full repayment is placed.

zh: 这种掠夺如何运作？当下与未来的关系——对把“经济”理解为支配装置至关重要——提供了双重攫取模式，我们将在下文补充第三种。第一，通过财产权或其他权力关系确立对未来资产可靠控制的人，享有稳定的租金、销售款、股息或债务偿还流。然而，正如我们在
以及

所探讨的，未来收入主张的持有者不必等待未来。如果该主张得到可靠确立，并有法律和市场装置支持——尤其是使主张能够轻易、即时地从一人转让给另一人、因而具有“流动性”的装置——所有者就可以转让他人并立即获得意外之财。每一次主张的转移，例如公司股份交易或衍生品形成时，都会增加一个向未来提出索取的人。第二，也是更有助于理解经济及其表面增长的，购买未来收入主张的人通常可以按折扣获得它。重复前几章的例子：一年后可得的 100 美元收入——来自股息、销售或租金——今天可能以比如 90 美元购得。从未来获得的付款之折价，反映了在确立它时被设计进去的延迟或推迟，以及通过使其提前可用的机制所产生的溢价。购买未来收入，使 90 美元得以在一年内看起来“增长”超过 10%，变成 100 美元。
en: How does the predation work? The relation between present and future – essential to grasping the ‘economy’ as an apparatus of domination – offers a double mode of capture, to which we will add a third, below. First, those who establish a viable hold on future assets, through rights of property or other power relations, enjoy a steady stream of rents, sales, dividends, or debt repayments. However, as we explored in
and again in

, the possessor of the claim to future revenue does not have to await the future. If the claim is reliably established and supported with legal and market devices, especially devices that make the claim easily and instantly transferable from person to person, and thus ‘liquid’, the owner can transfer it to others and enjoy an immediate windfall. Each successive transfer of the claim, as when corporate shares are traded, or when derivatives are formed, creates an additional claimant on the future. Second, and more important for making sense of the economy and its apparent growth, those who then purchase the claim to future revenue can typically acquire it at a discount. To repeat the example from previous chapters, an income of $100 available in a year’s time – from dividends, sales, or rents – might be purchased today for, say, $90. The discounted price of a payment acquired from the future reflects the delay or postponement engineered in establishing it, and the resulting premium generated through the mechanism that makes it available in advance. The purchase of a future revenue allows the $90 to appear to ‘grow’, over the course of a year, by more than 10 per cent, into the sum of $100.

zh: 我们栖居的世界不是由作为结构的资本主义、而是由作为过程的资本化所界定的。推迟的工程依赖于暴力、掠夺、基础设施、法律和流动性等形式，正是它催生了货币资本的可能性本身，赋予其奇特的增长力量。因此，货币不仅是便利交换或储存财富的手段，更是凭借推迟的秩序、主要作为一种对未来货物或收入的主张而被生产出来的。换言之，货币几乎总是信用货币：它总是指涉并索取更远的东西。它主要由私人商业银行发行（有政府担保作为后盾），所组织的不仅是交换
或储存，还有对未来施加负担。由于推迟的效力、它所促成的贴现过程，以及货币创造被限制在私人的、营利性银行和金融公司手中（如我们在

所见），货币的生产伴随着对“利息”收费的权力。（我们通常说货币“赚取”利息，把其增值能力自然化。）几乎所有货币都是信用，而所有信用，由于有按复利收取利息的权力，都必须偿还，且成本呈指数增长。例如在 3% 的利率下，货币成本二十四年翻倍；在 6% 下则十二年翻倍。但这只是另一种说法：那些制造信用货币、或能够获得信用货币制造能力的人，可以按折扣购买未来——十二年后可得的 100 美元收入，今天可以按 50 美元的折价购得。
en: We inhabit a world that is defined, not by capitalism as a structure, but by capitalising as a process. The engineering of postponement, dependent on forms of violence, predation, infrastructure, law, and liquidity, gives rise to the very possibility of money capital, awarding it its curious power to grow. Thus, money is not merely a means to facilitate exchange or to store wealth, but is produced, thanks to the order of postponement, mainly as a claim on a future good or revenue. Money, in other words, is almost always credit money: it always refers to and claims something further. Issued largely by private commercial banks (backed by government guarantees), it organises not merely exchange

or storage, but the encumbering of the future. Thanks to the effectiveness of postponement, the process of discounting that it enables, and the restricting of money creation to private, profit-making banks and financial firms, as we saw in

, the production of money comes with the power to impose a charge for ‘interest’. (We commonly refer to this as the money ‘earning’ interest, naturalising its ability to increase.) Almost all money is credit, and all credit, due to the power of charging interest, at a compound rate, has to be repaid, at a cost that increases exponentially. At 3 per cent, for example, the cost of money doubles in twenty-four years; at 6 per cent, in twelve years. But this is just another way of saying that those who manufacture or have access to the manufacturing of credit money can purchase the future at a discount – an income of $100 available twelve years from now can be purchased today at the discounted price of $50.

zh: 利率和贴现率是描述同一现象的两种方式，从同一架望远镜的两端观看（重提前一章的光学隐喻）。利率从当下向前看，计算一笔现款在未来某点的价值。贴现率从未来那一点出发向后推算，计算如果考虑到货币价值随时间“增长”的能力，那笔未来款项今天值多少。在一种循环推理过程中，一个概念常常用另一个概念来解释。于是，对未来收入价值的贴现被归因于货币赚取利息的“自然”过程。但事实上这一切都不是自然的。两种比率都源于权力关系，以本书探讨的所有方式。可靠地主张未来资产的权力——依赖于推迟的安排以及排除或减少他人主张的能力——与通过银行体系“汇集”这类主张使其流动的机制相结合，就是能够在当下出售该主张的来源。
未来主张出售时的折扣，随后被归因于货币赚取利息的力量，而不是归因于这些攫取、推迟和汇集的机制。
en: The interest rate and the discount rate are two ways of describing the same phenomenon, seen from opposite ends of the same telescope (to repeat the optical metaphor from the previous chapter). The interest rate looks forwards from the present and calculates the value of a present sum of money at a future point. The discount rate starts from that future point and works backwards, calculating what that future sum would be worth today if one allowed for the power of money to ‘grow’ in value over time. In a process of circular reasoning, one concept is often explained in terms of the other. Thus, discounting the value of future income is ascribed to the ‘natural’ process by which money earns interest. But none of this, in fact, is natural. Both rates arise from relations of power, in all the ways this book has explored. The power to reliably claim a future asset, dependent on the arrangement of postponement and the ability to exclude or reduce the claims of others, combined with the mechanism that ‘pools’ such claims through the banking system to make them liquid, is the source of the ability to sell the claim in the present.
The discount at which the future claim is sold is then ascribed, not to these mechanisms of capture, postponement, and pooling, but to the power of money to earn interest.

zh: 我们关于货币或资本的朴素日常观念——标准经济理论所复制的一种观念——有助于遮蔽这种攫取未来的过程。标准观点不把资本视为对未来付款的控制形式，而如我们在
所见，视为从过去储蓄起来的资金。人们想象这些储蓄存放在银行里，银行再贷给企业家，通常用于投资“机器”或“技术”以赚更多钱。在一些
想象中，以及在许多经济学家的模型中，机器本身成为“资本”的代表。利息支付于是可以被描述为付给那些表面上的“储蓄”被用来增长更多财富者的报酬——而不是享有国家授予的特权和保护、垄断信用创造的金融机构所收取的租金。
en: The obscuring of this process of capturing the future is aided by our naive, everyday conception of money or capital, a conception reproduced in standard economic theory. The standard view thinks of capital not as a form of control of future payments but, as we saw in

, as funds saved up from the past. These savings are stored in banks, it is imagined, which then lend them to entrepreneurs, typically to invest in the ‘machinery’ or ‘technology’ required to make more money. In some

imaginations, and in many economists’ models, the machinery itself comes to represent ‘capital’. The payment of interest can then be described as the reward paid to those whose apparent ‘savings’ have been used to grow more wealth – rather than the rent charged by the financial institutions that, thanks to their state-granted privileges and protections, monopolize the creation of credit.

zh: 事实上，除了为组织主张者带来的收益和按折扣购得主张所得的利润之外，还存在第三种由支配未来而产生的攫取模式。随着未来变得更确定或面临更多风险，对未来付款的主张在价值上始终可能发生波动。当然，风险可能反映一个资本化主张可能崩溃，摧毁对未来的权力所创造的全部资本。更常见的是，随着主张因银行、货币市场和各种计算装置的扩展而变得更具流动性，利润可以来自购买主张本身价值的涨跌前景，而非主张本身。于是，由基础资产衍生的流动性本身，可以成为被攫取的资产。如
所指出的，这类“衍生品”本身并不新鲜。1970 年代以来，一套类似物理学家熟悉的“热”方程、用纸笔推导出的定价公式——布莱克—斯科尔斯—默顿模型——的运用，使人们有可能把附着于任何金融工具的风险与基础资产分开“定价”。这些衍生品的价值不一定计算得十分精确，但足以令人信服，从而能够以更大规模把这类风险作为资产营销。
随着其制造增加，从“套利”中获利的机会也成倍增加，套利指“同一”事物在不同时间或不同地点价格的差异。正如罗伯特·迈斯特所解释的，制造流动性本身的梯度，成为这种差异的来源，从而成为攫取剩余之机会的来源。
与所有此类攫取一样，大部分收益将作为贡赋或税收强加于人，如我们在前几章所见，由生产、使用或维护未来资产——其收入已被攫取——的人支付。
en: There is, in fact, a third mode of capture that arises from the command of the future, besides the gain for those who organise the claim and the profit from acquiring it at a discount. Claims to future payments are always open to fluctuations in value, as the future becomes more certain or more subject to risk. Of course, the risk may reflect the fact that a capitalising claim might collapse, destroying the entire capital that a power over the future created. More frequently, as a claim becomes more liquid, thanks to the building out of banking, money markets, and calculative devices, profits can be made by purchasing, not the claim itself, but the prospect of its increase or decrease in value. Thus, the liquidity itself, derived from the underlying asset, can become an asset to be captured. Such ‘derivatives’, as pointed out in

, are in themselves nothing new. The deployment from the 1970s of a pricing formula similar to the ‘heat’ equation familiar to physicists, and worked out with pen and paper, the Black–Scholes–Merton model, made it possible to ‘price’ the risk attached to any financial instrument separately from the underlying asset. The value of these derivatives was not necessarily calculated with great accuracy, but with sufficient persuasiveness to allow marketing such risks as assets on an even larger scale.

As their manufacture increases, the opportunities multiply to profit from ‘arbitrage’, meaning the difference in price of the ‘same’ thing at different moments in time or different locations. Manufacturing the very gradients in liquidity, as Robert Meister explains, becomes the source of this difference, and thus of the opportunity to capture surplus.

As with all such capture, the majority of the gain will be imposed as a tribute or tax, as we saw in earlier chapters, to be paid by those who produce, use, or maintain the future asset whose revenue has been captured.

zh: 这种金融资产的增殖没有在“经济”的计算中得到恰当衡量。但这并不降低经济生产的用处。恰恰相反，即使经济作为多数人福祉的衡量越来越不适当，由于这一点以及我们提到的所有其他原因，它作为稳定力量反而愈加重要，因为它保障了可预测的未来
，而资本化和贴现越来越依赖这样的未来。事实上，正如迈斯特所示，在 2007—8 年全球金融危机之类的事件中，“经济”可能“爆炸”的风险，恰恰成为那些从风险买卖中获利者可以挥舞的威胁。迈斯特建议，更好地理解这种炸毁经济的威胁，以及“经济”的稳定效果对金融业所代表的未被计算的价值，可以为更民主地质疑攫取未来的权力提供基础。
en: This proliferation of financial assets is not properly measured in calculations of ‘the economy’. But this does not reduce the usefulness of the production of the economy. On the contrary, even as the economy becomes less appropriate as a measure of most people’s wellbeing, for this and all the other reasons we have mentioned, it grows in importance as a stabilising force that secures the predictable future

on which capitalising and discounting increasingly rely. Indeed, as Meister shows, the risk that the ‘economy’ might ‘explode’ becomes, in episodes such as the 2007–8 global financial crisis, precisely the threat that can be wielded by those who profit from the buying and selling of risk. A better understanding of this threat to blow up the economy, and the uncounted value that the stabilising effect of ‘the economy’ represents for the financial industry, Meister suggests, could provide the basis for a more democratic contestation of the power of the capture of the future.

zh: 把资本化作为一个过程来关注，可以避免许多关于未来攫取模式增殖之研究面临的陷阱——那些通过金融化观念把握这些模式的研究。越来越多人的生活受到日益沉重的债务负担支配：在许多全球南方国家，债务主要在国家层面产生，并通过政府紧缩计划强加于个体家庭；而在多数全球北方国家，则主要发生在个人层面。在后者中，住房抵押贷款、学生贷款、汽车租赁、信用卡、私人医疗费用以及育儿和养老费用——所有这些都使生活的很大部分成为一份持续且不断扩大的还款时间表。
然而，金融化观念通常依赖于金融与“实体”经济之间的区分。我们很快就会看到，真实之物与纯粹金融之物之间的这种区分，是经济发明所产生的最强大效果之一。这一效果与其说通过区分两者来运作，不如说通过变出对金融的极其片面的理解——脱离刚刚描述的所有推迟和产品制造工作——以及同样片面的实体概念来运作。
en: The focus on capitalising as a process allows one to avoid the pitfall that faces many studies of the proliferation of modes of capture of the future – those that grasp them through the idea of financialisation. The lives of increasing numbers of people are governed by the growing burden of debt, whether incurred predominantly at the national level in many countries of the South, and imposed on individual households through programmes of government austerity, or mainly at the personal level, in most countries of the North. Among the latter, home mortgages, student loans, car leases, credit cards, private healthcare charges, and the costs of childcare and elder care – all these set up so much of life as a continuous and expanding repayment schedule.

However, the notion of financialisation usually depends on a distinction between finance and the ‘real’ economy. We will see shortly how this distinction between what is real and what is merely financial is one of the most powerful effects produced by the invention of the economy. The effect operates not so much by distinguishing the two, but by conjuring a very one-sided understanding of finance, divorced from all the kinds of work of postponement and product manufacture just described, and an equally one-sided conception of the real.

zh: 金融化所表达的，我们已能看到只是更广泛过程的一个方面。占主导地位的剩余攫取装置以真实、物质的方式运作，把人和物质的依赖关系安排为“资产”，从中获得持续的投资收入。
这种攫取不仅通过公开的负债形式进行，还通过支配工作生活、电力、水和其他基础设施供应、社交媒体、娱乐、旅行和休闲、医疗等等——所有这些都日益处于投资者所有或股东所有企业的原则之下；并通过把许多国家的住房转变为难以负担的资产，抵押贷款还款占收入的份额越来越大。在这些安排下，每一个攫取未来
付款的过程——从抵押贷款到租金，从公用事业费到娱乐订阅，从高等教育学费到医疗费用，再到各种消费购买——都成为一项资产，被资本化并转化为收入流，供投资者在当下按折扣获得，由未来按全价偿还——利润作为收费强加给后来的使用者。
en: Financialisation expresses what we can already see to be only one aspect of a wider process. The dominant apparatuses for the capture of surplus operate in real, material ways, by arranging human and material dependencies as ‘assets’ from which a continuous investment income is derived.

The capture works not only through overt forms of indebtedness, but through the command of working life, the supply of electrical power, water, and other infrastructure, social media, entertainment, travel and leisure, healthcare, and more, all increasingly under the principle of investor- or shareholder-owned firms; and by the transformation of housing in many countries into unaffordable assets, for which the mortgage payments consume an ever-larger share of earnings. Under these arrangements, every process of capturing future

payments, from mortgages to rents, utility charges to entertainment subscriptions, higher education fees to medical costs, to every kind of consumer purchase, becomes an asset, capitalised and converted to an income stream, available to investors at a discount in the present, to be repaid at full price from the future – a profit imposed as a charge on later users.

zh: 此外，当下生活对多数人来说日益被偿还先前攫取款的重负所累。与此同时，多少拥有资产的家庭——例如能够付清购房款、或通过退休基金建立股市股份所有权的人——开始依赖这些资产价值的上涨，无论是通过房价上涨还是股票价值飙升。由于就业收入水平很少能补偿资本化资产所强加的更高收费，扩大一个家庭资产的价值成为增加财富的主要手段，从而抬高下一代住房和其他服务的成本。即使是中等富裕者，也因此被鼓励通过强化以后来者为代价的生活方式，来保护自己的生活水平。
en: Life in the present, moreover, is increasingly burdened for the majority with the repayment of earlier extractions. Meanwhile, households with some access to assets, such as those able to pay off the cost of purchasing a home or to build ownership of shares in stock markets through retirement funds, come to depend on the inflation of the value of such assets – whether through rising house prices or booming share values. With levels of income from employment seldom compensating for the increased charges imposed by capitalised assets, expanding the value of a household’s assets becomes a principal means of increasing wealth, thereby raising the cost of housing and other services for the next generation. Even the modestly well-off are thus encouraged to protect their own standard of life through the intensification of methods of living at the expense of those who come later.

zh: 更好的明天
en: Better Tomorrows

zh: 2011 年，美国最高法院取消了商业公司对竞选进行独立支出的限制。它们如今可以通过政治行动委员会（PAC）汇集无限资金。这些所谓的“超级政治行动委员会”开始协调企业付款，并代表企业开展政治竞选。美国电视喜剧演员斯蒂芬·科尔伯特用这一裁决作讽刺，自己成立了一个政治行动委员会，名为“为了明天会更好的美国人，明天”。“开国元勋们会希望是这样的，”他在电视节目中庆祝这一举动时说，“前提是他们创建的是
，而不只是一个国家。”这一讽刺把两个主题连接起来：当凡勃伦甚至在一个世纪前就已指认的“主导制度”——商业公司——施加非凡影响时，政治生活的问题；以及一种关于推迟的政治修辞。这种修辞通过许诺更美好的未来来承诺福祉和改善，但其效果是延期。这种延期就是我所说的增长的托词。
en: In 2011, the US Supreme Court removed the restrictions on independent spending on elections by business corporations. They could now pool their unlimited funds through political action committees, or PACs. The new super PACs, as they became known, began to coordinate corporate payments and run political campaigns on their behalf. The US television comedian Stephen Colbert parodied the Supreme Court decision by setting up a political action committee of his own, named Americans for a Better Tomorrow, Tomorrow. ‘It’s the way [the] founding fathers would have wanted it,’ he said, celebrating the event on his television show, ‘if they had founded

, instead of just a country.’ The parody connected two themes: the problem of political life when extraordinary influence is exercised by what Veblen, even a century earlier, had already identified as its ‘master institution’, the business corporation; and a political rhetoric of postponement. The rhetoric promises well-being and improvement through the pledge of a better future, but its effect is one of deferral. This deferral is what I have referred to as the alibi of growth.
body.review: 校注：底本此处将美国最高法院取消公司独立竞选支出限制的裁决记为2011年。美国联邦选举委员会所载Citizens United v. FEC裁决日期为2010年1月21日；这与后文科尔伯特在2011年的讽刺活动是不同时间节点。正文保留底本年份。 https://www.fec.gov/updates/citizens-united-v-fecsupreme-court/ https://www.fec.gov/law/litigation/cu_sc08_opinion.pdf

zh: 你如何组织和控制一个建立在剥夺未来之上的社会秩序——在其中，当下本身因先前的掠夺而贫困化，而建立哪怕中等财富的唯一手段就是参与同一个剥夺过程？你如何能不断许诺明天会更好，明天？答案是，你建立起一种所谓的效果，称之为经济，并把与未来的关系——即使掠夺和贫困化的过程在扩张——改写为其“增长”的必然运动。这种对资产资本化以及经济作为政治—技术效果的理解，将使我们更好地把握“经济”是如何以及为何被发明的。要理解经济作为治理装置的作用，我们必须先简要回顾资本化的较长历史、它所产生的过度，以及二十世纪中叶管理这些过度的较早方法的崩溃。如我们将会看到，经济作为治理装置的创造，为那场崩溃提供了回应。
en: How do you organise and control a social order built upon the deprivation of the future, in which the present is itself impoverished by previous predations, and the only means of building even moderate wealth is to participate in the same process of deprivation? How do you keep promising a better tomorrow, tomorrow? The answer is that you establish, as it were, an effect called the economy and recast the relationship to the future – even as the processes of predation and impoverishment expand – as the inevitable movement of its ‘growth’. This understanding of the capitalising of assets, and of the economy as a politico-technical effect, will allow us to better grasp how and why the ‘economy’ was invented. To understand the role of the economy as an apparatus of government, we must first briefly recap the longer history of capitalisation, the excesses to which it gave rise, and the collapse in the mid-twentieth century of earlier methods of managing that excess. The creation of the economy as an apparatus of government, as we will see, provided a response to that collapse.

zh: 首先，回顾。资本化未来收入的方法本身并不新近。今天所谓的金融化资本主义——这些技术也许更为普遍——并非在根本上不同于工业资本主义，也不同于先于它的商业资本主义。甚至在一千年前，如我们在
和
所讨论的，法蒂玛和马穆鲁克时期埃及的商人就与统治家族合作，按类似原则管理农民缴税。变化的是这一过程发生的规模，以及攫取、资产化和资本化未来收入所凭借的装置。
en: First, the recap. Methods of capitalising future revenue are not in themselves recent. Today’s so-called financialised capitalism, where these techniques are perhaps more widespread, is not somehow fundamentally distinct from industrial capitalism, or the commercial capitalism that preceded it. Even a millennium ago, merchants in Fatimid and Mamluk Egypt, as we discussed in
and

, collaborated with the ruling household to manage tax payments by farmers on similar principles. What has changed is the scale on which the process happens, and the apparatuses through which future revenues are captured, assetised, and capitalised.

zh: 在这个伊斯兰世界的边缘，在近代早期的欧洲，未来收入的资本化最广泛地设计于远距离贸易中——一种殖民和奴隶制秩序，其运作不仅是为了供应货物，更是为了通过商业和奴隶制产生信用货币，主要形式是汇票。货物和被奴役者的运输和销售，是这种从信用中攫取剩余的装置。如
所探讨的，该体系的危机促成了另一种信用装置——工业工厂——的发展。
en: On the periphery of that Islamic world, in early modern Europe, the capitalising of future revenues was engineered most extensively in longdistance trade, a colonial and slave-based order that operated not simply to supply goods, but to generate credit money, through commerce and slavery, mainly in the form of bills of exchange. The shipping and sale of goods and enslaved persons was the apparatus for this capture of surplus from credit. A crisis in that system, as
explored, led to the development of a different credit apparatus, the industrial factory.

zh: 十八世纪末、十九世纪初工业资本主义的出现，应以一种新方式理解。制造业并不代表与商业和信用世界的根本断裂。更重要的是，把雇佣劳动强制投入煤矿和工厂，使我们能以出奇清晰的形式看到信用创造问题，而“经济”是这一问题后来的解决方案。
经济的发明是对一个有着更长历史的挑战——如何确保和稳定信用货币的生产——的二十世纪回答。
en: The emergence of industrial capitalism, in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century, should be understood in a new way. Manufacturing did not represent a fundamental break with the world of commerce and credit. More than that, the forcing of wage labour into coal mines and factories enables us to see in surprisingly clear form the problem of credit creation, for which ‘the economy’ was a later solution.
The invention of the economy was a twentieth-century answer to a challenge that had a longer history – how to secure and stabilise the production of credit money.

zh: 甚至工厂生产和煤矿开采也是一种资本化方法——一种通过信用货币的精心构建而对未来进行掠夺的形式。把生产转入机械化、后来用煤作动力的工厂，提出了一个独特问题：如何向大量工人支付周薪或月薪——在日常交易很少使用实体货币（硬币或金银）的背景下，几乎所有付款都通过账面信用、期票和汇票处理。如我们所见，支付工资结果不是一个问题，而是一个机会——也许甚至成为把劳动力集中到工厂的主要优势。在没有铸币的情况下支付工人的常见办法，是所谓的“实物工资制”。商人—制造商用账簿上的信用记录、或代金券和筹码支付工资。这些可以在当地商店兑换货物，商店往往属于同一个商人。商人可以从货物制造成本与雇员必须支付的购买价格之间的差额中获利，也可以从这类安排的其他方面获利：消费品的垄断供应；收取利息；通过预先向工人提供必需品、然后按全价记在账上的方式使工人负债；以及提供住房，其租金也从工资中扣除。在按信用支付的劳动与信用货币以购买或租金收费形式返还商人之间，正是这段延迟时间成为利润来源。这使实物工资制和账面信用具有高度剥削性，并导致试图限制它们的法律获得通过。
en: Even factory production and coal mining were a method of capitalisation – a form of predation on the future through the elaboration of credit money. The diverting of production into mechanised and later coal-powered factories presented a singular problem: how to pay large numbers of workers a weekly or monthly wage – in a context in which physical money (coin or specie) was little used in everyday transactions, almost every payment being handled through book credit, promissory notes, and bills of exchange. As we saw, the payment of wages turned out to be not a problem but an opportunity – perhaps even becoming a main advantage of concentrating workforces into factories. A common solution for paying workers in the absence of coinage was the system of ‘truck’, as it was called. The merchant-manufacturer paid wages with a credit entry on his books, or with chits or tokens. These could be exchanged for goods at local shops, often owned by the same merchant. Merchants could profit from the difference between the cost of making goods and the price at which the employee had to purchase them, and from other aspects of such arrangements: a monopoly on the supply of consumption items; the charging of interest; the indebting of workers by providing them with necessities in advance that were then charged on the books at full price; and supplying them with housing whose rent was also deducted from wages. The very delay in time between the work that was being paid on credit and the purchase or rental charge with which the credit money was returned to the merchant was a source of profit. This made the use of truck and book credit highly exploitative and led to the passing of laws in an attempt to restrain them.

zh: 立法并没有消除这种通过信用榨取的机器。可以说，今天的雇佣劳动仍然是一种实物工资制。其显著特征是工人仍然以信用货币获得报酬。工资支付形式从商人信用或代币变为纸币，再变为薪金支票，今天则是银行账户之间的电子转账。但工资仍然作为信用货币而产生。而且可以说，它们仍然依赖“公司商店”，信用货币通过公司商店连本带息地返还银行体系。
en: Legislation did not eliminate this machinery of extraction through credit. Wage labour today, one might say, is still a truck system. Its distinctive feature is that workers are still paid in credit money. The form of the wage payment changed from merchant credit or tokens to banknotes, then to paychecks, and today to electronic transfers between bank accounts. But wages are still brought into being as credit money. And they still depend, so to speak, on the ‘company store’ through which the credit money is paid back into the banking system, with interest.

zh: 然而，这家商店不再只是同一个商人控制的单独店铺。它现在是更庞大信用装置的一部分，
即一整套话语性和非话语性装置，它们组织对工资的攫取，不是通过店铺或市场的简单装置，而是通过产品设计、贸易展、时尚、广告、品牌创造、消费者咨询和比较等技术。
这些机制早在十八世纪就伴随着制造业的发展，为富裕和中产阶层出现。

今天，经由互联网及其界面、平台、社交媒体网站和网红的改造，它们构成了庞大装置，工薪阶层通过它偿还“借来”的工资。工人为商品、服务及其营销广告支付的价格，包含贷款的加价——即对使用货币的收费，资本化货币体系正是依靠这种收费运作。这些界面和平台本身如今成为少数公司的主要利润来源，这些公司最近超过主要全球石油公司（沙特阿美除外），成为世界上资本化估值最高的公司——亚马逊、苹果、Alphabet 和 Meta。这些公司的收入来自对在线广告、数据和电子商务的近乎垄断，日益控制着“商店”的准入，借出的工资正是通过商店被重新捕获。事实上，这些云端巨型企业不仅依赖用户为在线商品和服务付费，还依赖用户生产这些“封地”所拥有的数据。因此，云端用户第二次贡献了自己的劳动，这一次是无偿的，甚至还要支付订阅费。他们的在线互动、浏览、购买和反应，既把自己生产为消费的欲望主体，也生产了巨型企业拥有并资本化的关于这些自我的海量数据。
en: However, the store is no longer just a single shop under the control of the same merchant. It is now part of a much larger credit apparatus,

namely the array of apparatuses, discursive and non-discursive, that organise the capture of wages, not through the simple device of a shop or marketplace, but through the technologies of product design, trade shows, fashion, advertising, brand creation, consumer advice, and comparison.
These mechanisms were already appearing in the eighteenth century, for the well-to-do and the middling classes, in tandem with the development of manufacturing.

Today, transformed by the internet, with its interfaces, platforms, social media sites, and influencers, they constitute the vast apparatus through which wage earners repay their ‘loaned’ wage money. The prices workers pay for goods, services, and their marketing and advertising include the mark-up for the loan, the charge for the use of money upon which a capitalising monetary system operates. The interfaces and platforms are themselves now the main source of profit for the handful of corporations that recently surpassed the major global oil firms (other than Saudi Aramco) as the most highly capitalised companies in the world – Amazon, Apple, Alphabet, and Meta. With revenues arising from the near monopoly of online advertising, data, and e-commerce, these firms increasingly control access to the ‘store’ through which loan wages are recaptured. Indeed, the cloud-based megacorporations rely upon their users not only to pay for online goods and services, but to produce the data that these ‘fiefdoms’ own. Thus, users of the cloud contribute their labour a second time, in this case unpaid or even at the cost of a subscription charge. Their online interacting, browsing, purchasing, and reacting manufactures both themselves as the desiring subjects of consumption and the vast data on those selves that the megacorporations own and capitalise.

zh: 早期工业体系中商人银行家创造信用与今天运作的安排之间的差异在于，从十九世纪中叶起，政府引入法规将制造商与银行家、工作场所与银行分开。事实上可以认为，从该世纪下半叶起在世界工业化地区开始出现的那种经济生活形式的独特要素，不再仅仅是工人与生产资料所有权的分离，也不只是生产与市场的表面分离，或所谓经济与政治的分离。它是工作场所和消费场所与货币来源的分离。以前既控制货物制造和营销方式、又提供信用的商人，被分成组织货物
者和创造货币者。而且，不仅是货物制造和零售依赖信用供给，同样，信用的制造也依赖不断扩展的大规模就业体系，并进而与广告、品味塑造和消费相结合，这些今天日益被企业拥有的云端所垄断。
en: The difference between the creation of credit by the merchant banker of the early industrial system and the arrangements operating today is that from the mid-nineteenth century governments introduced regulations to separate manufacturer and banker, workplace and bank. In fact, one could argue, the distinctive element of the form of economic life that began to emerge in the industrialised regions of the world from the second half of that century was no longer simply the separation of workers from the ownership of the means of production, nor the apparent separation of production from the market, nor the so-called economic from the political. It was the separation of the places of work and consumption from the source of money. Merchants who had previously combined the control of how goods were made and marketed with the supply of credit were separated into those who organised goods

and those who created money. And it was not simply that the manufacturing and retailing of goods depended upon a supply of credit, but equally that the manufacturing of credit depended on a widening system of large-scale employment, combined in turn with advertising, taste-making, and consumption, with these increasingly monopolised today by the corporate-owned cloud.

zh: 现代货币是银行生产的信用货币。今天银行创造了流通中 95% 以上的货币，几乎全部是银行体系内账户之间的数字转账。银行制造信用货币的能力，取决于一项合理保证：被指定为信贷的资金，日后将在创造它们的体系内被重新指定为购买的还款。事实上，银行发行的“票据”——无论是以钞票、支票还是电子账簿条目的形式——如果不存在通过购买货物、服务、订阅和其他租金来返还它的要求，就不会作为货币运作。
en: Modern money is bank-produced credit money. Banks today create more than 95 per cent of the money in circulation, almost all of it as digital transfers between accounts within the banking system. The ability of banks to manufacture credit money depends upon a reasonable guarantee that the funds designated as credit will later be redesignated within the system that creates them as repayments for purchases. In fact, the ‘paper’ issued by a bank, in the form of notes, cheques, or electronic ledger entries, would not function as money if there were no requirement to return it through the payment for goods, services, subscriptions, and other rents.
body.review: 校注：底本“95%以上”未在本段标明地区、时期和货币统计口径。英格兰银行2014年说明中，97%指当时英国广义货币中的银行存款份额；这一常被引用的比例不能直接当作所有国家、所有货币口径的恒定比例。正文保留原数，未作全球比例复算。 https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/quarterly-bulletin/2014/quarterly-bulletin-2014-q1

zh: 然而，银行不能只在内部制造货币。要成为真正的资产，银行制造的货币必须经过某种攫取装置，债务人通过该装置向债权人转移一份增量。因此，以工资形式贷出的货币，是相对于工资必须花在其上的购买和收费而被生产并产生效果的。只有对未来支出的保证，才能使银行资产创造得以进行。
信用货币只能作为技术和物质安排的一部分运作，在这种安排中，货币在未来某一点被花掉，并连本带息“返还”银行。对于制造出来支付工资的货币，利息支付不是作为单独费用强加给工人，而是内置于商品价格、服务收费和住房成本之中。这些价格、收费和成本在 GDP 计算中被衡量时，既包括产品的价值，也包括作为企业利润和对作为工资创造的信用货币之利息而强加的附加费。
en: However, banks cannot just manufacture money internally. To become a real asset, bank-made money must pass through some apparatus of capture, through which the debtor transfers an increment to the creditor. Thus, the money loaned out in the form of wages is produced and given effect in relation to the purchases and charges on which the wage must be spent. Only the guarantee of that future spending enables the bank’s creation of assets to proceed.

Credit money can operate only as part of a technical and material arrangement where at a future point the money is spent, and ‘returned’ to the bank with interest. With the money manufactured to pay wages, the interest payment is not imposed on the worker as a separate fee, but is built into the prices of commodities, the charges for services, and the cost of housing. These prices, charges, and costs, measured in the calculation of GDP, include both the value of the product, and the surcharge imposed as corporate profit and interest on the credit money created as wages.

zh: 经济取代黄金成为“不变标准”
en: The Economy Replaces Gold as the ‘Invariant Standard’

zh: 这种通过信用机制攫取剩余的能力——在时间中设置一道间隙，把当下与未来、劳动与其产品的购买、从而贷款与偿还分隔开来——并不限于工业体系和雇佣劳动。确切地说，正如

所提出的，现代工业是一个绕道。货物制造——涉及艰苦劳动、低利润率以及持续的竞争威胁——很快让位于其他攫取装置，这些装置更长期、更少受竞争威胁，尤其是那些通过重新增强的帝国扩张力量运作的装置，包括修建铁路、公用事业、土地开发计划和住房抵押贷款，以及较旧的攫取形式，特别是征收政府税。如前面几章所探讨的，所有这些都作为创造信用的装置运作：确立一种特定的可靠未来付款流——租金、票价、运费、公用事业费、税收和抵押贷款还款——然后在当下出售对这些未来付款的主张。现代股份制公司与帝国扩张一道出现，成为制造和动员这类主张的主要装置。随后，甚至先前主要由家族企业或合伙企业主导的工业生活，也按同一原则重组，采用股份制公司的形式，以便把未来收益资本化并从中获利。
en: This ability to capture surplus through a credit mechanism, by setting up a gap in time that separates present from future, labour from the purchase of its products, and thus loan from repayment, was not limited to the industrial system and wage labour. If anything, as

proposed, modern industry was a detour. The manufacturing of goods – involving hard work, low margins, and the constant threat of competition – soon gave way to other apparatuses of capture, which were more long-term and less subject to threats of competition, especially those operating through the renewed powers of imperial expansion, including the building of railways, utilities, land development schemes, and housing mortgages, alongside older forms of capture, in particular the imposing of government taxes. All of these, as explored in previous chapters, operated as apparatuses to create credit, by establishing a particular stream of reliable future payments, in the form of rents, fares, freight charges, utility bills, taxes, and mortgage payments, and then selling claims upon those future payments in the present. The modern joint-stock company emerged, in tandem with imperial expansion, as a principal device for the manufacture and mobilisation of such claims. Subsequently, even industrial life, previously the preserve mainly of family-owned businesses or partnerships, was reorganised on the same principle, adopting the form of the joint-stock company in order to capitalise and profit from future earnings.

zh: 然而，创造信用以购买这些特定未来主张，与创造信用以支付工资之间，仍然存在差异。以公司股份或政府、公司和抵押债务等形式出售对特定收入的索取，被理解为出售“金融”产品。这类安排明确按照从未来攫取收入的原则运作，形式是股息、利息支付或其他用钱赚钱的方式。支付工资似乎以不同方式运作。它似乎属于一个“实体”世界，而不是金融世界；在实体世界中，支付工资所需的货币只是生产成本。尽管存在这种表面差异，金融产品和工资都依赖信用货币的创造；在信用货币创造中，确保可靠的未来支出和资金返还，是货币体系的基础。
en: There remained a difference, however, between the production of credit to purchase these specific claims on the future and the production of credit to pay wages. The selling of claims to specific revenues, in forms such as company shares or government, corporate, and mortgage debt, was understood as the sale of ‘financial’ products. Such arrangements operated explicitly on the principle of capturing income from the future, in the shape of dividends, interest payments, or other modes of using money to earn money. The payment of wages seemed to operate differently. It appeared to belong to a ‘real’ world rather than a world of finance, in which the money required to pay wages was simply a cost of production. Despite this apparent difference, both financial products and wages depended on the creation of credit money, in which securing a reliable future expenditure and a return of the funds was the basis for the monetary system.

zh: 要使现代货币创造体系运转，仅把企业与银行分开还不够。私人银行业需要一种手段，使其付款承诺能够作为公共货币发挥作用。这需要现代国家的权力来担保这些承诺。这种权力并非通过国家干预、监管和担保私人信用货币体系而产生，而是通过私人商业银行与公共或准公共中央银行及政府的共同演化而产生。资本主义货币与
监管权力共生发展；现代银行业与现代政府相互塑造。
en: To make the modern system of money creation work, it was not enough to separate businesses from banks. Private banking required a means of enabling its promises to pay to function as public money. This required the powers of the modern state, to guarantee those promises. Such powers came into being, not by the state intervening to regulate and guarantee the private system of credit money, but through the coevolution of private commercial banks and public or quasi-public central banks and governments. Capitalist money and the power of
regulation developed symbiotically; modern banking and modern government formed one another.

zh: 这种共同发展有两个要素。英格兰提供了典范案例，尽管英国商人银行家借鉴了荷兰人、以及更早的地中海商人和帝国城邦所发展的金融创造与治理方法。
en: This codevelopment had two elements. England provides the paradigmatic case, although English merchant bankers drew upon methods of creating and governing finance previously developed by the Dutch, and before them by merchants and imperial city-states in the Mediterranean.

zh: 第一，通过有利可图的殖民贸易和奴隶贩卖积累起来的私人货币创造，获得了公共形式。十七世纪末，伦敦有权势的商人邀请荷兰商人银行家的盟友奥兰治亲王威廉入侵英格兰。威廉依赖他们获得新王位，并率领这个国家卷入其四百年来首次在欧洲进行的重大战争；他接受了一项安排：商人们组建新的股份制公司——英格兰银行——为战争提供信贷。这些战争越来越以扩张英国海外商业垄断为目的，而为战争筹集的贷款不再要求一年内偿还。它们被赋予“国家”债务的新形式（而非君主的私人债务或殖民地贸易公司的商业债务），并由关税和消费税的指定收入担保，尤其是酒类和烟草税，而穷人不成比例地承担这些税负。通过出售对这些未来国家收入的折扣主张，商人银行家如今可以创造有公共担保的私人信用货币。
早在“民族国家”出现之前，“民族”就被变了出来——被生产为承载这笔战争债务义务的人为躯体。
en: First, private money creation, built up through profitable colonial trading and slaving ventures, was given a public form. At the end of the seventeenth century, powerful merchants in London invited an ally of the Dutch merchant bankers, Prince William of Orange, to invade England. Dependent on them for his new throne and leading the country into its first major war in Europe in 400 years, William accepted an arrangement where the merchants formed a new joint-stock company, the Bank of England, to provide credit to fund the war-making. The loans for wars, fought increasingly to expand English overseas commercial monopolies, no longer required repayment within the year. They were given the new form of ‘national’ debt (rather than a private debt of the monarch, or a commercial debt of the colonial trading companies) and were guaranteed by hypothecated revenues from customs and excise, especially duties on alcohol and tobacco, paid disproportionately by the poor. Selling discounted claims to those future state revenues, the merchant bankers could now create private credit money with a public guarantee.
Well before the emergence of the ‘nation-state’, the ‘nation’ was conjured into being – produced as the artificial body upon which this obligation for war debts was imposed.

zh: 第二，该银行获得贴现私人汇票和发行见票即付银行票据的垄断权。

当工业就业的增长催生小型地方银行时，它们发行的票据只能在伦敦贴现，由英格兰银行担保所有私人创造的信用货币在最后关头都能兑换为金镑——尽管在实践中，英格兰银行按折扣接受地方银行纸币，交换的不是金币，而是它自己的纸币，后者逐渐具有了国家纸币的性质。纸币可按固定比率兑换为具有市场价值的贵金属黄金这一原则，产生了起作用的虚构：所有银行创造的信用货币，其价值都来自一种作为基础的国家商品货币。黄金价格的稳定产生了一种
看似价值“标准”的东西，即金本位，据说它支配着可发行纸币的数量。然而事实上，在银行货币新体系下，工人工资的支付依赖于这种由准公共国家银行支持的私人货币创造安排。信贷名义上以黄金储备为担保，但在实践中，担保来自国家对维持英格兰银行盈利能力及其纸币可靠性的保证，而这一保证又通过银行对“国家”未来税收的主张来实现。
私人信用货币的创造，如今通过广泛的雇佣劳动和大规模消费体系运作，并由其与公共征税权力的联系来担保。
en: Second, the bank was granted a monopoly on the discounting of private bills of exchange and the issuing of bank bills payable on demand.

When the growth of industrial employment brought into being small provincial banks, the notes they issued could be discounted only in London, with the Bank of England guaranteeing that all privately created credit money could be redeemed, in the last resort, in gold sovereigns – although in practice the Bank accepted local banknotes at a discount in exchange not for gold coins but for its own notes, which gradually took on the character of a national paper currency. The principle that paper notes were convertible at a fixed rate to gold, a precious metal with a market value, gave rise to the working fiction that all bankmade credit money derived its value from an underlying national commodity-money. The stability of the price of gold generated what

appeared as a ‘standard’ of value, the gold standard, that supposedly governed the quantity of paper money that could be issued. In fact, however, the payment of workers’ wages, under the new system of bank money, rested on this arrangement of private money creation backed by a quasi-public national bank. The credit was secured notionally against reserves of gold, but, in practice, against the state’s guarantee of maintaining the profitability of the Bank of England, and the reliability of its notes, through the bank’s claim on ‘the nation’s’ future tax payments.
The private creation of credit money, now operating through the extensive system of wage labour and mass consumption, was secured by its connection to the public power of taxation.

zh: 尽管有这种担保，私人银行创造信用货币的不断扩大的权力仍必须进一步加以管理，以限制私人信用创造容易引发的危机。当大型金融投机失败，或长期战争带来对税负和未来消费稳定性的更广泛不确定性时，情况尤其如此。在实践中，只有英国实行金本位，其他主要货币的价值通过国际贸易与英镑挂钩，而大部分贸易由伦敦融资。
最终，在二十世纪两次世界大战之间的政治和经济危机中，金本位的虚构崩溃了。英格兰银行和其他国家银行被迫放弃黄金储备代表国家货币价值所依赖之不变标准的主张。
en: Despite this guarantee, the widening power of private banks to create credit money had to be further managed, to limit the crises to which private credit creation was prone. This was especially the case when large financial speculations failed, or when prolonged warfare brought wider uncertainty about tax burdens and the future stability of consumption. In practice, only Great Britain operated on a gold standard, with the value of other major currencies tied to sterling through international trade, most of which was financed through London.

Eventually, in the political and economic crises of the interwar decades of the twentieth century, the fiction of a gold standard collapsed. The Bank of England and other national banks were forced to abandon the claim that reserves of gold represented the invariant standard on which the value of national money was based.
body.review: 校注：底本“只有英国实行金本位”的说法须区分制度采用与国际货币体系中英镑的主导地位。1876年美国外交文书明确记载德国采用黄金作为单一本位，并自1876年1月1日起以金马克为法定货币；因此不能将此句理解为其他国家从未采用金本位。正文保留作者论述，未擅自改写其关于国际信用体系的解释。 https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1876/d67

zh: 战后时期，不变“标准”被重新发明，办法是设计一个新的参照物：“经济”。实物工资制的一般化安排——工资以私人制造的信用货币支付——不能再依赖黄金储备的虚构，即以此作为确立货币价值、限制信用创造的手段。相反，货币秩序将通过生产一个可预测的未来来稳定，其形式是关于经济指标的“客观知识”。
国民收入账户体系本是战时用于规划军备生产的装置，战后被改用于管理信用的生产。对国民收入或 GDP 及其增长率、价格通胀、就业水平和利率的估算，提供了一组数字；对数字的解释取代黄金，确立了让私人货币创造得以进行的信用度。通过增长指标和其他“宏观经济”指标，中央银行如今可以监管和限制信用货币的创造，
也可以限制工资要求和价格上涨。经济通过这些衡量技术被生产为一个自身存在的对象，已成为如今从未来榨取所依赖的工具。
en: The invariant ‘standard’ was then reinvented in the postwar period by devising a new referent: ‘the economy’. The generalised arrangement of truck, in which wages were paid in privately made credit money, could no longer depend on the fiction of reserves of gold as the standard establishing the value of money and the means of placing limits on the creation of credit. Instead, the monetary order would be stabilised by the production of a predictable future, in the form of the ‘objective knowledge’ of economic indicators.

A wartime device for planning the production of armaments, the system of national income accounts, was repurposed after the war as the means of managing the production of credit. The estimating of national income or GDP and its rate of growth, and of price inflation, employment levels, and interest rates, provided a set of numbers whose interpretation established, in place of gold, the creditworthiness that allowed the private creation of money to proceed. Through the metric of growth and other ‘macroeconomic’ indicators, central banks could now regulate and place limits on the creation of

credit money – as well as on wage demands and price increases. Produced through these techniques of measurement as an object in itself, the economy had become the instrument on which extraction from the future would now depend.

zh: 金融与实体
en: The Financial and the Real

zh: 也许有用的是，不仅把它理解为经济，还通过与杰里米·边沁全景敞视监狱的松散类比——福柯曾把它用作权力运作的图表——把它理解为“经济全景装置”。与全景敞视监狱一样，它是一种通过调节身体和组织欲望的方式产生知识形式的装置。作为不变标准，经济从来不可能只是对物质现实的再现，或只是统计制品、一组真理。它作为控制装置在物质层面运作，分解并重组人、家庭、材料、欲望和未来，产生稳定、结构和客观性的效果。
en: It may be useful to think of this arrangement not simply as the economy, but, by loose analogy with Jeremy Bentham’s Panopticon, deployed by Foucault as a diagram of the operation of power, as the EconoCon. Like the Panopticon, it is a device that produces forms of knowledge, through ways of regulating the body and organising desire. To operate as an invariant standard, the economy could never just be a representation of a material reality, or just a statistical artefact or set of truths. It operated materially, as an apparatus of control, decomposing and recomposing persons, households, materials, desires, and futures, creating an effect of stability, structure, and objectivity.

zh: 要以这种方式运作，经济需要若干特征。这些要求使我们理解，经济衡量或再现福祉方式中的“缺陷”为什么不是有待识别、修正或取代的疏忽，而是其政治效力的关键。它们解释了为什么在气候危机面前，我们无法摆脱“增长”的动力。
en: To work in this way, the economy required a number of features. These requirements allow us to understand how the ‘flaws’ in the way the economy measures or represents well-being are not oversights, to be identified, revised, or replaced, but the key to its political effectiveness. They explain our inability, in the face of the climate crisis, to escape the dynamic of ‘growth’.

zh: 第一，经济必须组织当下与未来之间的关系本身。它做到这一点，不是通过衡量诸如信用或资本化这类通过生产未来、延迟和绕道而运作的动态过程，而是通过按固定时间间隔组成一系列静态图像，然后把它们叠加起来比较差异。经济是按年度快照计算的，而不是某种能够衡量跨时间建构之关系的东西。这种静态形式允许为每一年计算一个单独总量，然后与前一年和后一年比较。如我们在
所见，快照的序列就是可作为“增长”衡量的东西。对经济来说，当下与未来不是一种内在时间性展开中的时刻，而是同一种政治技术的共时产物。
en: First, the economy must organise the very relation between present and future. It achieves this, not by measuring dynamic processes, such as credit or capitalisation, that operate through the production of futures, delays, and detours, but by composing a series of static images, at regular intervals in time, then superimposing one upon the next to compare their difference. The economy is calculated as an annual snapshot, not as something that can measure relations constructed across time. This static form allows a separate total to be calculated for each year, which can then be compared with the previous year, and the following. As we saw in

, the sequence of snapshots is what is measurable as ‘growth’. For the economy, present and future are not moments in the unfolding of an internal temporality, but coeval products of a political technology.

zh: 第二，为使这些快照可以比较，必须赋予难以捉摸的“技术”因素以决定作用。当把一年的国民账户与下一年比较时，数字会

按通胀进行调整。这需要判断货物或服务成本上升反映的是“实际”变化还是仅仅“货币”变化。一次医疗程序、一部手机、住房、娱乐订阅或优步行程的成本上升，应归因于某种技术改进，代表产品的“实际”增加，还是仅仅是价格通胀，须予折减以只衡量经济的“真正”增长？这一判断必须对经济生活的每个部门和每类产品作出。从国民收入核算的最初阶段起，这就被认为是一项“无法克服”的挑战，而且随着时间推移越来越如此，因为产品性质和品质的微小变化不断增加。
没有任何先验规则能作出这一判断。相反，必须就“技术”变化的贡献作出一系列临时判断。
技术改进似乎提供了解释增长的力量或动量。在实践中，它为从未来榨取提供了越来越普遍的托词。
en: Second, to make these snapshots comparable, a determining role is given to the elusive factor of ‘technology’. When the national accounts for one year are compared with those for the next, the figures are

adjusted for inflation. This requires deciding whether the increased cost of a good or service reflects a ‘real’ change or merely a ‘monetary’ change. Is the increased cost of a medical procedure, a mobile phone, accommodation, an entertainment subscription, or an Uber ride attributable to some technical improvement, representing a ‘real’ increase in the product, or is it merely price inflation, to be discounted so as to measure only the ‘actual’ growth of the economy? This determination must be made across every sector of economic life, and for every category of product, a challenge that from the very beginnings of national income accounting was recognised as ‘insuperable’, and progressively so, since minor variations in the nature and qualities of products increased through time.
No a priori rule can make the determination. Rather, a series of ad hoc judgements must be made about the contribution of a change in ‘technology’.
Technical improvement appears to provide the force or momentum that accounts for growth. In practice, it provides an increasingly pervasive alibi for extraction from the future.

zh: 第三，以 GDP 衡量的经济由“产品”组成。与资本主义等较早的术语相比——资本主义被理解为投机性的、金融驱动的、与帝国主义纠缠在一起、本质上不稳定的——经济把集体生活再现为本质上稳定的，因为它是“生产性的”。它衡量和再现物质关系时，不是依据投机性投资、不平等的财产关系、不稳定的资本流动和货币变动，而是依据产品的流通，即价格被汇总以估算 GDP 的商品。具体而言，它衡量经济“价值”的生产——其基础是计算人们在新东西上花了多少钱，形式是货物和服务。这种“产品”充当可据以创造信用货币的未来。没有它，几乎不可能有任何货币。
en: Third, the economy, measured by GDP, is composed of ‘products’. In contrast to older terms like capitalism, understood as speculative, finance-driven, bound up with imperialism, and essentially unstable, the economy renders collective life as essentially stable, because it is ‘productive’. It measures and represents material relations not in terms of speculative investment, unequal relations of property, unstable flows of capital, and currency movements, but as the circulation of products, meaning the commodities whose prices are aggregated to estimate GDP. It is a measure, specifically, of production of economic ‘value’ – based on counting how much people spend on new stuff, in the form of goods and services. This ‘product’ functions as the future against which credit money can be created. Without it, there could scarcely be any money.

zh: 经济被配置为“产品”的领域，铭刻了一种区分：产品被视为物质的，货币则被视为仅仅是衡量和比较其价值、并购买它们的手段。尽管货币的存在方式主要是通过它所购买的货物和服务而产生，因而只能物质地存在，而不是作为财富储存，经济仍把物质与货币呈现为两个分离的领域，一个被视为实在，另一个被视为非实在或虚构。这种区分被视为理所当然，而没有被理解为经济生产的效果——而且它继续影响甚至非常出色的“金融化”研究。
en: Configured as a realm of ‘products’, the economy inscribes a distinction: between products, considered material, and money, considered simply as a means to measure and compare their values, and to purchase them. Even though money exists largely, not as a store of wealth, but as something effected through the products and services on which it is spent, and thus as something that can exist only materially, the economy presents the material and the monetary as separate realms, one rendered real and the other nonreal or fictitious. This distinction is taken for granted, rather than understood as an effect of the production of the economy – and continues to inform even very capable studies of ‘financialisation’.

zh: 产品与价格、物质与货币之间的区分，本身是不断被制造出来的东西。它是经济衡量的结果，而不是有待衡量的先在现实。可以从历史角度理解这种相互强化，但从更具分析性的角度看，既可以从物质方面、也可以从货币方面来看。在物质方面，正如米歇尔·卡隆向我们展示的，我们所谓的产品实际上更像过程，而不是事物。

例如，一辆汽车是由设计、评估、性能、欲望、依恋、维修和过时等持续操作组装而成的，更不用说道路、燃料、车辆贷款、交通法规、许可证和治安管理，没有这些，“产品”就无法作为价值物存在。此外，在大多数国家，被衡量为经济的产品中，有一半到四分之三甚至不像汽车那样呈现为物质事物。它们属于所谓的服务类别，最初是一个剩余类别，如今却成了一个笼统术语，指构成“经济”主要部分的过程、依恋、义务、付款和表演的增殖。经济在这里的作用不是衡量物质世界及其增长，而是把这种异质性化解为看似实在的事物及其价格。
en: The distinction between product and price, between the material and the monetary, is itself something continually manufactured. It is an outcome of the measurement of the economy, not a prior reality to be measured. This mutual reinforcement can be appreciated from a historical angle, but in more analytical terms it can be seen both from the side of the material, and from the side of money. On the material side, on the one hand, as Michel Callon shows us, what we call products are actually more like processes than things.

A car, for example, is assembled out of ongoing operations of design, evaluation, performance, desire, attachment, repair, and obsolescence, not to mention the arrangements of roadways, fuels, vehicle loans, traffic laws, permits, and policing without which the ‘product’ could not exist as an item of value. In most countries, furthermore, between half and three-quarters of the products that are measured as the economy, unlike a car, do not even present themselves as material things. They fall into the category of so-called services, originally a residual grouping but now a catchall term for the proliferation of processes, attachments, obligations, payments, and performances that constitute the major part of ‘the economy’. The economy functions, here, not to measure the material world and its growth, but to resolve this heterogeneity into what appears as real things and their price.

zh: 另一方面，货币不是实在之物的对立面。金融并非与生产性相分离，原因很简单：货币作为信用关系，总是涉及一种物质化手段。虽然几乎所有货币都是在银行中通过开立信贷额度和相应借记创造的，但如果没有未来的物质过程、某种攫取付款的装置，使货币得以实现并产生，这一单独的会计行为就不会有效力。因此，购买住房的抵押贷款只有通过房屋的存在才能作为货币运作：贷款的偿还和利息费用可借房屋收取和强制执行，同时还涉及设计、规划监管、产权、治安管理、分区、种族隔离和红线划界以及止赎等过程，住房的价值正是通过这些过程被生产和担保。
同样，企业支付工人所需的信用货币，只有存在某种此后信用货币工资必须花在其上的企业产品，才能作为支付手段运作。金融这种混合形式——既是当下的信用付款，又是伸向未来、强制偿还的物质装置——正是
经济的生产作为治理当下与未来之安排的模式所确保的东西。
en: Money, on the other hand, is not the opposite of what is real. The financial is not something separate from the productive, for the simple reason that money, as a relationship of credit, always involves a means of materialisation. While almost all money is created in banks by opening a line of credit and corresponding debit, that individual act of accounting would have no effectiveness if there were not a future material process, some apparatus for capturing payment, through which the money were to be realised, and brought into being. Thus, a mortgage loan to purchase a house functions as money only through the presence of a house on which repayments of the loan and the interest charge can be collected and enforced, along with the processes of design, planning regulation, property rights, policing, zoning, racial segregation and redlining, and foreclosure through which the value of housing is produced and guaranteed.

Likewise, the credit money that a business firm requires to pay its workers can function as a means of payment only if there is some business product on which that credit money wage must later be spent. This hybrid form of finance, as credit payment in the present and as an apparatus built out into the future that compels repayment, is what the production of the
economy, as a mode of governing the arrangement of present and future, secures.

zh: 生产实在与金融之间的差异需要工作。它被内置于经济的衡量本身。如我们刚刚所见，对每一种产品和服务的衡量，都必须在其成本的“实际”成分与纯粹“货币”成分之间作出判断。更重要的是，以 GDP 衡量的经济排除了金融产品的制造和购买成本，如股票、债券和衍生品；在最近一次国民账户重新校准中，其中一些不再被归类为成本，而被归类为最终“产品”。
它还排除资产价值升值所产生的收入——即资本利得——因为资本利得通常不在年度快照中体现。这一未被衡量的过程占国民收入高达 25%，其中大部分流向极富者，但对于维持哪怕是中等富裕也日益重要。
en: Producing the difference between the real and the financial requires work. It is built into the very measurement of the economy. As we have just seen, for the measurement of every product and service, a decision must be made between the ‘real’ component of its cost and the merely ‘monetary’. More than this, the economy as measured by GDP excludes the cost of the manufacture and purchase of financial products, such as stocks, bonds, and derivatives, some of which, in a recent recalibration of national accounts, were requalified not as costs but as final ‘products’.

It also excludes income arising from the appreciation of the value of assets – that is, capital gains – because capital gains are not usually visible in an annual snapshot. This unmeasured process represents as much as 25 per cent of national income, the bulk of it going to the very rich, but increasingly important to maintaining even moderate forms of affluence.

zh: 反过来，国民收入账户确实包括对非生产性活动的付款，只要这些活动广泛存在并可被视为一种“服务”。例如，住房租金被视为对住房服务的付款，即使房屋是多年前或几十年前建造的，租金与建造结构——提供服务——的原始成本毫无关系，而只是垄断土地财产准入者所强加的收费。奇怪的是，自住业主在国民账户中被认为获得了等值收入。他们被估算为享有住在自己房子里的“服务”。（因此，人类再生产和家庭中的其他无酬劳动不被计入，但房子本身却因
生产性的“劳动”——为所有者提供住所——而在国民账户中得到承认。）
en: Conversely, the national income accounts do include payments for unproductive activities, if they are widespread and can be considered a ‘service’. For example, the payment of rent for housing is considered a payment for housing services, even if the home was built years or decades before, and the rent has no connection to the original cost of building the structure – of providing the service – but is merely a charge imposed by those who monopolise access to landed property. Curiously, owners who occupy their own homes are considered in the national accounts to be receiving an equivalent income. They are imputed to enjoy the ‘service’ provided by the opportunity to live in their own house. (So reproductive and other unpaid household labour of humans is not counted, but the house itself is recognised in the national accounts for the
productive ‘labour’ of housing its owners.)

zh: 财产租金和利息并不是从被建构为“生产性”经济之组成部分的资产控制中榨取付款的唯一模式。经济衡量的最重要特征是，甚至物质货物和有用服务的成本也包含一笔可观的金融收费。例如在德国，估算表明日常商品价格的 35% 至 40% 是制造商和供应商向银行及其他债权人支付利息的成本。
这种从未来大量且不断扩张的利息收入榨取，作为成本转嫁给货物和服务的最终消费者，已成为经济“增长”的一个重要组成部分。
en: Property rents and interest are not the only modes of extracting payment from the control of assets construed as part of the ‘productive’ economy. The most important feature of the measurement of the economy is that even the cost of material goods and useful services includes a significant financial charge.
